name: Waiter Sweep
description: The Waiter Sweep elevates a controlled leg from deep half guard and manages the opponent's posts so the bottom player can tip the base and come on top.
summary: The Waiter Sweep elevates a controlled leg from deep half guard and manages the opponent's posts so the bottom player can tip the base and come on top.
overview:
The bottom player is underneath the opponent's hips in deep half guard with one leg available to be lifted and supported. The waiter leg shelf and deep-half hip position distinguish this sweep from a generic underhook wrestle-up. The landing may retain half guard; side control requires clearing the legs.

Bring the shoulder under the hip while controlling the leg and protecting the exposed arm. Shift the opponent's weight enough to make the controlled leg available for elevation. Support the lower leg with the arm and shoulder connection while using the legs to help lift.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Lucas Valle — waiter sweep from deep half](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LzphtRQwv6g); [Ryan Hall — the Waiter Sweep](https://ryanhallonline.com/p/waiter-sweep).

attacker.name: Waiter Sweep Attacker
attacker.description: Waiter Sweep (attacker): Bring the shoulder under the hip while controlling the leg and protecting the exposed arm. Shift the opponent's weight enough to make the controlled leg available for elevation.
attacker.overview:
The bottom player is underneath the opponent's hips in deep half guard with one leg available to be lifted and supported. The waiter leg shelf and deep-half hip position distinguish this sweep from a generic underhook wrestle-up. The landing may retain half guard; side control requires clearing the legs.

Bring the shoulder under the hip while controlling the leg and protecting the exposed arm. Shift the opponent's weight enough to make the controlled leg available for elevation. Support the lower leg with the arm and shoulder connection while using the legs to help lift.

Use an appropriate sleeve grip in gi or a suitable arm connection without assuming the same grip exists in no-gi. Coordinate leg elevation and post control rather than trying to bench-press the opponent. Follow the hips to a stable top position; pass the remaining leg only if that separate opening exists.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

In Valle's gi demonstration, the collar connection manages the upper body while hip movement brings the lifted leg into the waiting hand; control of the posting sleeve then assists the reversal. Keep the head protected from a crossface as you move underneath. Once on top, establish hip control and balanced chest pressure for the actual landing before beginning a separate pass.

Manage the posting arm: Use an appropriate sleeve grip in gi or a suitable arm connection without assuming the same grip exists in no-gi.
Tip the controlled base: Coordinate leg elevation and post control rather than trying to bench-press the opponent.
Come up and settle: Follow the hips to a stable top position; pass the remaining leg only if that separate opening exists.

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (bottom): Where should your shoulder go to establish deep half?
flashcards.answer: Bring the shoulder under the hip while controlling the leg and protecting the exposed arm.
flashcards.answer_line: Under the opponent's hip while you control a leg

plausible: Beside the hip with your shoulder outside their thigh
Under the lower shin with your head outside the knee
trap: Under their chest with both hips beyond your reach

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (bottom): Why shift the opponent's weight before lifting the leg?
flashcards.answer: Shift the opponent's weight enough to make the controlled leg available for elevation.
flashcards.answer_line: To make the controlled leg light enough to elevate

plausible: To keep their full weight on the leg you plan to lift
To make the arm shelf unnecessary once they lean
trap: To lift before their weight can leave the controlled foot

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (bottom): What forms the waiter shelf?
flashcards.answer: Support the lower leg with the arm and shoulder connection while using the legs to help lift.
flashcards.answer_line: Arm and shoulder supporting the elevated lower leg

plausible: Your hand beneath the heel while your shoulder stays clear of the leg
Your shoulder beside the thigh with the lower leg still on the mat
trap: Your forearm across the shin while your shoulder stays outside

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (bottom): In Valle's gi version, which grip captures the posting arm?
flashcards.answer: Use an appropriate sleeve grip in gi or a suitable arm connection without assuming the same grip exists in no-gi.

plausible: A collar grip alone with the posting arm free
Both hands remaining under the elevated leg
trap: A trouser-cuff grip while the supporting hand remains free

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (bottom): What must cooperate to tip the base?
flashcards.answer: Coordinate leg elevation and post control rather than trying to bench-press the opponent.
flashcards.answer_line: Leg elevation and control of the available post

plausible: Arm strength alone with the hips motionless
Releasing the lifted leg while pulling the collar
trap: Lifting the leg while the tipping-side hand remains free

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (bottom): You come on top with a leg still caught. What next?
flashcards.answer: Follow the hips to a stable top position; pass the remaining leg only if that separate opening exists.
flashcards.answer_line: Stabilize top half guard before a separate pass

plausible: Count side control without freeing the leg
Reach across to the far shoulder while abandoning hip control
trap: Pull the caught leg out before establishing top balance

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (bottom): What distinguishes the starting hip relationship?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player is underneath the opponent's hips in deep half guard with one leg available to be lifted and supported.
flashcards.answer_line: You are beneath their hips with one leg available to lift

plausible: Beside their hips with the controlled leg left on the mat
Under their shoulders with both legs beyond your reach
trap: Facing their chest from shallow half with your head outside

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (bottom): Why is an underhook wrestle-up alone not the waiter mechanism?
flashcards.answer: The waiter leg shelf and deep-half hip position distinguish this sweep from a generic underhook wrestle-up. The landing may retain half guard; side control requires clearing the legs.
flashcards.answer_line: The elevated leg shelf is a separate defining control

plausible: An underhook supplies the same shelf beneath the opponent's lower leg
Standing up on the underhook fixes the same elevated-leg angle
trap: Driving forward from the knees duplicates lifting the captured leg

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (bottom): The knee cannot follow the lifted leg freely. What should you do?
flashcards.answer: Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.
flashcards.answer_line: Release the restraint instead of twisting through it

plausible: Raise the shelf farther before freeing the knee
Change your hip angle while keeping the foot clamped
trap: Relax only the sleeve grip while maintaining the leg restraint

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (bottom): How does hip movement help build Valle's shelf?
flashcards.answer: Hip and leg movement bring the opponent's lower leg into the hand and onto the shoulder support.
flashcards.answer_line: It brings the controlled leg into the supporting hand

plausible: It moves your shoulder away while the leg stays on the mat
It brings the far knee down while your shelf arm remains outside
trap: It lifts your torso while the supporting hand loses the lower leg

defender.name: Waiter Sweep Defender
defender.description: Waiter Sweep (defender): A deep-half player supporting your elevated leg is setting the waiter mechanism. Preserve hand or foot support before the opponent controls the tipping direction.
defender.overview:
The bottom player is underneath the opponent's hips in deep half guard with one leg available to be lifted and supported. The waiter leg shelf and deep-half hip position distinguish this sweep from a generic underhook wrestle-up. The landing may retain half guard; side control requires clearing the legs.

A deep-half player supporting your elevated leg is setting the waiter mechanism. Preserve hand or foot support before the opponent controls the tipping direction. Avoid leaving the hips directly above an established deep-half shoulder connection.

Return the elevated leg only while the knee can move without twisting. Accept a controlled reversal if balance is lost rather than risking a shoulder or knee. Use inside frames and the remaining leg connection if the opponent comes on top.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

An early escape withdraws the elevated leg or restores a usable post before your weight is carried over the bottom player. If you land underneath, recover frames and knees instead of trying to hold the original standing base through the reversal.
key_principles: Recognize the leg shelf: A deep-half player supporting your elevated leg is setting the waiter mechanism.
Keep an available post: Preserve hand or foot support before the opponent controls the tipping direction.
Manage hip position: Avoid leaving the hips directly above an established deep-half shoulder connection.
Recover the leg early: Return the elevated leg only while the knee can move without twisting.
Fall without a locked-arm post: Accept a controlled reversal if balance is lost rather than risking a shoulder or knee.
Retain guard on landing: Use inside frames and the remaining leg connection if the opponent comes on top.

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (top): Which cue identifies the waiter threat?
flashcards.answer: A deep-half player supporting your elevated leg is setting the waiter mechanism.
flashcards.answer_line: A deep-half player supporting your elevated lower leg

plausible: A shallow half-guard player with your foot still bearing weight
A player below your hip with both arms outside the leg
trap: A player holding your ankle while their shoulder stays beyond your knee

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (top): What must you preserve before the tipping direction is controlled?
flashcards.answer: Preserve hand or foot support before the opponent controls the tipping direction.
flashcards.answer_line: A usable hand or foot post

plausible: Both hands committed to the same distant collar
Your lifted foot treated as the remaining base point
trap: A post on the side opposite the controlled tipping direction

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (top): Which hip position feeds the established shelf?
flashcards.answer: Avoid leaving the hips directly above an established deep-half shoulder connection.
flashcards.answer_line: Leaving your hips carried over the deep-half shoulder

plausible: Hips shifted outside their shoulder before the shelf settles
Hips behind a recovered leg with weight on a free post
trap: Hips withdrawn from their shoulder while the leg remains mobile

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (top): When can you safely recover the elevated leg?
flashcards.answer: Return the elevated leg only while the knee can move without twisting.
flashcards.answer_line: While the knee can follow without twisting

plausible: While your ankle is held but your pelvis can turn
When the sleeve releases although the knee stays wedged
trap: Once you can rotate the hip around the fixed lower leg

flashcards.question: Waiter Sweep (top): Once the reversal removes your base, what is appropriate?
flashcards.answer: Accept a controlled reversal if balance is lost rather than risking a shoulder or knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Follow the fall and rebuild frames underneath

plausible: Reach for a late hand post while retaining the old hip height
Keep the lifted foot fixed while turning your chest back down
trap: Stand the free leg up before securing any landing frame
